## Summary

Adds `--engine {vllm,sglang}` to the Model Explorer export CLI so a checkpoint's
device-partitioned architecture graph can be drawn from vLLM's or SGLang's own
pinned modeling source (instead of transformers'), with `--tp`/`--pp`/`--ep`
read from each engine's own sharding idioms.

- Whitelists `vllm-project/vllm` and `sgl-project/sglang` in `SourcePolicy`,
  pinned the same way `huggingface/transformers` already is
  (`vllm-project/vllm@v0.32.0`, `sgl-project/sglang@v0.5.22`).
- Documents `--engine`/`--tp`/`--pp`/`--ep` in `TraceLens/Visualizer/README.md`
  (the pre-existing partition flags were previously undocumented).

## Introspection fixes found validating against real MiniMax-M3 source

Running `--engine vllm --tp 2 --ep 4` against `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-flash`
exposed two genuine fidelity gaps (not engine-specific opacity — both are fixed
at the introspection layer so the real sparse-attention module is drawn, not
approximated):

1. **`block_tree.py`** — a side-feed chain's own producer (e.g. a fused `qkv`
   projection feeding a private `_run_attention` helper as a side input) was
   dropped from the segment list whenever it appeared in that chain, even when
   it also had an *independent, ordinary* forward consumer elsewhere in the
   same block (`qkv.new_zeros(...)`, `qkv.split(...)`). That silently dropped
   its node and tripped `DroppedSubmoduleProducerError`. Fixed by keeping the
   segment when the producer has an ordinary consumer.
2. **`extract.py`** — per-layer dense/sparse attention-class selection fell
   back to whichever class the AST last saw assigned, because the real
   choosing condition is an arbitrary free-function call it can't evaluate
   (`layer_id in _sparse_attention_layer_ids(config)`). Added recognition of
   the `sparse_attention_config.sparse_attention_freq` per-layer convention
   vLLM/SGLang use for this (same shape as the already-supported
   `moe_layer_freq` FFN convention) and resolve the attention class from it,
   so `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention` is correctly selected for every sparse layer.

Checked SGLang's `minimax_m3.py` too: it uses a single `MiniMaxM3Attention`
class gated by an `is_sparse_attention_layer` constructor flag rather than two
classes, so the class-misselection bug doesn't apply there; generation
succeeds without it.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/ModelUtils/ tests/Visualizer/` — 2438 passed.
- `black .` on all touched files.
- Generated and manually inspected both requested visualizations end-to-end:
  - `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-flash --engine vllm --tp 2 --ep 4`
  - `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-flash --engine sglang --tp 2 --ep 4`

  Both complete and correctly render `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention` as genuinely
  introspected sub-ops (not opaque) for all 60 layers.

+    ``model_executor/models/registry.py`` keeps several module-level dicts
+    (``_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS``, ``_MULTIMODAL_MODELS``, ...), each a literal
+    mapping of architecture name to a 2-tuple of strings. A few entries build
+    their value with a function call instead (dynamic defaults); those are
+    skipped, not guessed at.
+    """
+    try:
+        tree = ast.parse(text)
+    except SyntaxError:
+        return None
+    for node in tree.body:
+        if not isinstance(node, ast.Assign) or not isinstance(node.value, ast.Dict):
+            continue
+        parsed = _engine_literal(node.value)
+        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
+            continue
+        entry = parsed.get(architecture)
+        if (
+            isinstance(entry, tuple)
+            and len(entry) == 2
+            and all(isinstance(item, str) for item in entry)
+        ):
+            return entry
+    return None

+def _module_candidate_paths(module: str, template: str) -> list[str]:
+    """Where ``module`` (dotted or bare) lives, as subpaths relative to the repo root.
+
+    A bare name (``llama``) sits under the models package itself (``template``).
+    A dotted one (``vllm.models.minimax_m3``) names its own top-level package, a
+    file or, more often, a directory whose ``__init__.py`` re-exports the real
+    implementation (mirroring ``vllm.models.deepseek_v4`` and siblings).
+    """
+    if "." not in module:
+        return [template.format(module=module)]
+    as_path = "/".join(module.split("."))
+    return [f"{as_path}.py", f"{as_path}/__init__.py"]
+
+
+def _resolve_defining_file(
+    ref: GitHubRef, subpath: str, path: Path, architectures: set[str]
+) -> tuple[Path, str]:
+    """``(path, subpath)`` itself, or whichever sibling it re-exports from actually
+    defines the class.
+
+    A registry entry can point at a package ``__init__.py`` that only imports
+    the real implementation from a platform-specific neighbour (mirrors
+    ``vllm.models.minimax_m3`` re-exporting from ``nvidia/model.py``).
+    """
+    if not architectures or _defines_any_class(path, architectures):
+        return path, subpath
+    package = Path(subpath).parent
+    for module in _own_package_imports(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
+        relative = Path(*module.split("."))
+        for sibling_subpath in (
+            (package / relative).with_suffix(".py").as_posix(),
+            (package / relative / "__init__.py").as_posix(),
+        ):
+            sibling = fetch_github_file(ref, sibling_subpath)
+            if sibling is not None and _defines_any_class(sibling, architectures):
+                return sibling, sibling_subpath

+
+
+def _fetch_engine_file(
+    ref: GitHubRef, subpath: str, architectures: set[str]
+) -> Path | None:
+    """One engine source file -- or the real one it re-exports from -- plus its
+    own-package neighbours, all read at the same pinned commit."""
+    path = fetch_github_file(ref, subpath)
+    if path is None:
+        return None
+    _fetch_own_package(ref, subpath, path)
+    resolved, resolved_subpath = _resolve_defining_file(
+        ref, subpath, path, architectures
+    )
+    if resolved != path:
+        _fetch_own_package(ref, resolved_subpath, resolved)

+def _sglang_filename_candidates(config: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
+    """Model-type spellings to try under sglang's flat ``srt/models/`` layout.
+
+    Mirrors ``_config_model_types`` (outer wrapper first), plus each with one
+    trailing ``_text`` / ``_vl`` / ``_mtp`` component stripped -- sglang names
+    its file after the architecture family, not after transformers' internal
+    tower suffixes (``minimax_m3_text`` ships as ``minimax_m3.py``).
+    """
+    candidates: list[str] = []
+    for model_type in _config_model_types(config):
+        if model_type not in candidates:
+            candidates.append(model_type)
+        stem, _sep, suffix = model_type.rpartition("_")
+        if stem and suffix in {"text", "vl", "mtp"} and stem not in candidates:
+            candidates.append(stem)
+    return candidates

+def resolve_engine_modeling_files(
+    engine: str,
+    config: dict[str, Any],
+    *,
+    source_policy: SourcePolicy | None = None,
+) -> tuple[list[Path], list[str]]:
+    """vLLM / SGLang's own modeling file for this checkpoint, at a pinned release.
+
+    Resolves which file implements ``config``'s declared architecture inside
+    the chosen inference engine, the same way ``_transformers_github_modeling_file``
+    resolves one inside transformers -- a fixed tag, not the engine's main branch.
+    """
+    source = ENGINE_GITHUB_SOURCES.get(engine)

+        )
+    ref = parse_github_url(source)
+    policy = source_policy or get_source_policy()
+    if isinstance(policy, SourcePolicy):
+        policy.require_github_repo_allowed(ref.owner, ref.repo)
+    architectures = _declared_architectures(config) or {
+        str(name) for name in config.get("architectures") or []
+    }

+    if engine == "vllm":
+        registry = fetch_github_file(ref, VLLM_REGISTRY_SUBPATH)
+        registry_text = registry.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if registry else ""
+        for architecture in architectures:
+            entry = _vllm_registry_entry(registry_text, architecture)
+            if entry is None:
+                continue
+            module, _class_name = entry
+            for subpath in _module_candidate_paths(module, VLLM_MODELS_SUBPATH):
+                path = _fetch_engine_file(ref, subpath, architectures)
+                if path is not None:
+                    return [path], [ref.display]
+        return [], []
+
+    if engine == "sglang":
+        for candidate in _sglang_filename_candidates(config):
+            subpath = SGLANG_MODELS_SUBPATH.format(candidate=candidate)
+            path = _fetch_engine_file(ref, subpath, architectures)
+            if path is not None and _defines_any_class(path, architectures):
+                return [path], [ref.display]
+        return [], []

+    raise ValueError(
+        f"Unknown engine {engine!r}; expected one of {sorted(ENGINE_GITHUB_SOURCES)}"

+"""A ``self.<attr>`` built from a scalar LOCAL stays off the tensor edges.
+
+SGLang's attention settles its split sizes through an intermediate local
+before storing them on ``self``::
+
+    attn_tp_size = get_parallel().attn_tp_size
+    self.num_heads = self.total_num_heads // attn_tp_size
+    self.q_size = self.num_heads * self.head_dim
+    ...
+    q, k, v = qkv.split([self.q_size, self.kv_size, self.kv_size], dim=-1)
+
+``attn_tp_size`` can never be resolved to a concrete value (``get_parallel()``
+is an external, unresolvable call), and it is a bare local, not a
+``self.<attr>`` -- so ``self.num_heads``, and in turn ``self.q_size``, never
+qualified as a "scalar setting" and fell through as an unresolved TENSOR
+attribute, materialized as a Constant input wired straight onto the ``split``.
+The type-check then reported the split fed two tensor operands instead of one.
+"""

+from __future__ import annotations

+import ast
+import textwrap

+from TraceLens.ModelUtils.ast_analyze import (
+    _SCALAR_SETTING,
+    _self_config_values,
+)
+
+
+def _init(source: str) -> ast.FunctionDef:
+    tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(source))
+    cls = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef))
+    return next(
+        n for n in cls.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "__init__"
+    )
+
+
+_SPLIT_SIZE_VIA_LOCAL = """
+    class Attention:
+        def __init__(self, config):
+            attn_tp_size = get_parallel().attn_tp_size
+            self.total_num_heads = config.num_attention_heads
+            self.num_heads = self.total_num_heads // attn_tp_size
+            self.head_dim = config.head_dim
+            self.q_size = self.num_heads * self.head_dim
+            self.weight = weight
+"""
+
+
+class TestAScalarThreadedThroughAnUnresolvableLocal:
+    def test_the_local_dependent_attr_is_recorded_as_a_setting(self) -> None:
+        values = _self_config_values(_init(_SPLIT_SIZE_VIA_LOCAL), {})
+        assert values["num_heads"] is _SCALAR_SETTING
+
+    def test_an_attr_derived_from_that_attr_is_also_a_setting(self) -> None:
+        values = _self_config_values(_init(_SPLIT_SIZE_VIA_LOCAL), {})
+        assert values["q_size"] is _SCALAR_SETTING
+
+    def test_a_concretely_resolved_attr_still_resolves(self) -> None:
+        values = _self_config_values(
+            _init(_SPLIT_SIZE_VIA_LOCAL), {"num_attention_heads": 32, "head_dim": 128}
+        )
+        assert values["total_num_heads"] == 32
+

+        values = _self_config_values(_init(_SPLIT_SIZE_VIA_LOCAL), {})
+        assert "weight" not in values

+"""Every tensor packed into one tuple/list literal keeps a real consumer edge.
+
+SGLang's attention threads its split outputs through a plain tuple before
+handing them to the next method::
+
+    q, k, v = qkv.split([self.q_size, self.kv_size, self.kv_size], dim=-1)
+    inner_state = (q, k, v, forward_batch)
+    return None, forward_batch, inner_state
+
+A tuple/list literal used to resolve to only its LAST element with a real
+producer. ``inner_state``'s own producer came out as ``v`` -- so the graph
+drew ``split`` with a single consumer (whichever ordinal ``v`` happened to be),
+and the split's OTHER slices (``q``, ``k``) reported dead: nothing consumes
+them. Each distinct tensor packed into the tuple must be a real predecessor of
+whatever reads the tuple as a whole.

+import textwrap

+    PACK_LABEL,

+    )
